title: Ranzo's code, 1528: the letter to 'Garbino' (BnF fr. 3022 no. 20, Madrid 11 April 1528) and Hieronimo Ranzo's letters (fr. 2988 ff. 2, 9-10; DECODE R1894, R4450)

steps.what: Fetched fr. 3022 (Gallica btv1b90601558) and identified the three catalogue pieces and folios.
Found no. 10 already solved by Lasry (2023) with Tomokiyo's edited text (2026), and Lasry's 2026 preliminary decryption of Cipher 2 covering no. 6 and no. 19.
Transcribed no. 20 (1,315 groups) and ~2,600 groups of Ranzo's signed letters in fr. 2988; addition sheet transcribed (additione.json).
No. 20 code is initial letter + number, the number running in alphabetical order within each letter (solve.py, anchor.py).
Word annealer (solve2.py) on a held-out 3,900-word Castiglione control encoded the same way: ~46 % token, ~9 % type accuracy.
solve2.py on no. 20 + Ranzo: a stable function-word skeleton (che, il, per, non …) across six restarts; no content words.

Sought cribs: Clair. 327 and Clair. 314 copies (undeciphered), fr. 2988 other cipher pieces (a different French cipher), fr. 3019 no. 27 Ranzo letter (no decipherment), no duplicate text between no. 20 and Ranzo letters.
DECODE R1894 (catalogue 170) identified as the fr. 2988 Ranzo letter already transcribed; no key or decipherment on the record.

Contributed research history: George Lasry, collaborating with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, reconstructed a working Ranzo key from Norbert Biermann’s five-letter transcription. Selected values were checked against the historical addition. The Codex consolidation retains tentative proposals; this is dated source history, not work newly done on 14 October.

A Cryptoole alert (IT1520-1, solved 6 Oct 2026 by Paolo Rosson and George Lasry) led to Rosson's page and files (key/table.tsv, reading/islands.md, decode.py). Their reading uses this project's transcription for fr. 3022 no. 20 and fr. 2988, and a new transcription of the duplicate fr. 3019 ff. 73-74. No. 20 was not unread for lack of a key after all.

Applied Rosson's 779-value key (with his transcription corrections) to n20/f44r-f46v and ranzo_c006-c020. Groups with a value (sure, probable, null): no. 20 93.8%, R1894 (c017-c020) 97.2%; in runs of six or more sure/probable values: no. 20 79.8%, R1894 93.1%. Spot check: c017 and c020 decode as coherent 1528 Italian. Below the 95% bar on the connected-stretch measure; 84 groups of 3,903 have no value. Did not rerun their blind controls.

Prepared the Codex consolidation for contribution: reproduced 541 line-aligned readings, 6,428 cipher occurrences, all 871 key frequencies and two precisely bounded excerpts with translations. Checked the Cryptiana contemporaneous reports. Coverage includes hypotheses and is not measured plaintext correctness.

Split the combined catalogue item 7 target after George Lasry pointed out that it mixed different ciphers: del Vasto's no. 6 (Cipher 2, shifted letters with code groups; sibling no. 19) stays in vasto1527; no. 20 and the Ranzo letters (initial-letter code with numbered word lists) moved to ranzo1528; no. 10 (Cipher 1, read by Lasry and Tomokiyo, not reworked) is a cross-reference only. This folder takes no. 20, the Ranzo transcriptions, Rosson's measure and Lasry's contributed edition.

Tested George Lasry's correction that the addition sheet (fr. 3022 f. 50, additione.json) is not this code's key: of its 113 groups only g217 occurs (once) in the 3,912 transcribed groups of no. 20 and Ranzo's letters, and its numbers overlap the letters' own (b from 157 vs b up to 215 in the letters). The 18 Sept claim that it continues the base lists is withdrawn; page and NOTES corrected.

profile.documents extended to the five letters of George Lasry's package (fr. 2988 f. 2, fr. 2988 ff. 9-10 = R1894, fr. 3022 no. 20, fr. 4050 ff. 79-81, fr. 6638 pp. 67-70), counts from his counts.json; fr. 4050 and fr. 6638 not seen here.

George Lasry, by email: 'the Ranzo ciphers are solved Fr 2988 and Fr 20506 - my key or Rosson's key.' Fr. 20506 ff. 136-138 is the parallel copy of his letter 2 (fr. 2988 ff. 9-10, R1894; DECODE R4450), not a separately transcribed text.

measure_lasry.py: Rosson's key (with his g>214=s, t>196=r rule) applied to Lasry's Biermann transcription and compared token by token with Lasry's key. Where both value a token they agree on 94.4-96.3% per letter (spelling variants such as lettere/littere counted as agreement), including letters 4 and 5, which Rosson never saw. Bar measure per letter: fr. 2988 f. 2 96.2%, ff. 9-10 97.0% (read, with the copy fr. 20506), no. 20 94.4%, fr. 4050 87.7%, fr. 6638 89.0% (read in part); 5,974 of 6,428 overall (92.9%).

Outcome method changed from 'read from existing decipherment' to 'key recovered from ciphertext-only': Lasry's key was rebuilt from the ciphertext with cribs and structure (his NOTES and PR #35), and the addition sheet he spot-checked is another code; Rosson's key is a second, independent ciphertext-only recovery.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 6174 tokens, 936 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -1.992 per letter; random keys -2.454 (z 14.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.081 (mean -2.097, z 8.9); annealer on the real text -2.073. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.991; polyphony 0.0; 254 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.073

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry rebuilt his key from the ciphertext of Biermann's five-letter transcription with Italian cribs, repeated contexts and code-family structure (lasry/NOTES.md; PR #35); no decipherment, clear copy or key of these letters exists, and the 'Aditione nel zifra' he spot-checked is another code (1 of its 113 groups occurs here), so no external or adjacent plaintext supplied values. Paolo Rosson rebuilt a second key the same way, independently, on this project's transcription (6 Oct 2026); it agrees with Lasry's on 94-96% of the tokens both value, including letters 4 and 5, which Rosson never saw. This project's own annealer recovered only function words; its share is the transcription and the measurement.
outcome.fraction_read_source: measure_lasry.py on lasry/alignment.tsv (Biermann transcription, 6,428 cipher occurrences, five letters; fr. 20506 not counted twice), 18 Oct 2026: 5,974 of 6,428 read by the bar measure (presumed nulls, Lasry's stronger inferences, Lasry's tentative values matched by Rosson's key, Rosson's sure/probable values where Lasry has none). Per letter: fr. 2988 f. 2 96.2%, fr. 2988 ff. 9-10 (and its copy fr. 20506) 97.0%, fr. 3022 no. 20 94.4%, fr. 4050 87.7%, fr. 6638 89.0%. Lasry's own assignment coverage (tentative values included) is 95.9% of non-null occurrences.

gaps.item: fr. 3022 no. 20 (letter 3): 74 of 1,314 tokens not read by the bar measure (94.4%)
gaps.detail: 27 occurrences without a value in either key (Rosson's fills 37 of Lasry's 64 blanks) and 47 tentative values of Lasry's that Rosson's key does not match. Needs a comparison of both keys' readings with the images of ff. 44r-46v.

gaps.item: fr. 4050 ff. 79-81 and fr. 6638 pp. 67-70 (letters 4, 5): 191 and 105 tokens not read by the bar measure (87.7%, 89.0%)
gaps.detail: Lasry's key values 94.2% and 96.8% of them, but most tentative values cannot be confirmed: Rosson's key was built on letters 1-3 only. Not seen here; Biermann's transcription gives no Gallica link.

gaps.item: fr. 2988 ff. 2 and 9-10 (letters 1, 2, with the copies fr. 3019 and fr. 20506): 31 and 53 tokens open
gaps.detail: Scattered single code groups and tentative values; over the read bar.

outcome.notes: Key recovered from ciphertext-only by George Lasry (with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra) and, independently, by Paolo Rosson (with Claude), both 6 Oct 2026. Lasry, 16 Oct 2026: 'the Ranzo ciphers are solved Fr 2988 and Fr 20506 - my key or Rosson's key'. Measured here 18 Oct 2026: fr. 2988 (both letters) and its copy fr. 20506 meet the read bar; fr. 3022 no. 20, fr. 4050 and fr. 6638 are read in part. Split 14 Oct 2026 from targets/vasto1527.
